_comment: CRuby -> mruby API map for convert_mrbgem.rb. kind: call (rename; inject mrb as first arg when inject_mrb), macro (rename or identity, no mrb), expr (identifier replaced by an expression), type (identifier replaced), special (handled by converter code), refuse (no equivalent; marker left in output). needs_mrb marks identifiers that require an mrb_state in scope. Any CRuby-looking identifier missing from this file is refused by the converter.

type_check_refused._comment: Check_Type and rb_check_type (handler check_type in convert_mrbgem.rb) map a T_ name only when its entry has type_check exact or caveat. These names are refused with the reason given here.
type_check_refused.T_OBJECT: mruby's MRB_TT_OBJECT does not match CRuby's T_OBJECT: CRuby allocates exceptions as T_OBJECT (ruby4src error.c:3583 via object.c:118), mruby allocates them as MRB_TT_EXCEPTION (src/error.c:42), so the check would reject exceptions
type_check_refused.T_CLASS: mruby's MRB_TT_CLASS does not match CRuby's T_CLASS: a CRuby singleton class is a class with RUBY_FL_SINGLETON (ruby4src class.c:42), mruby allocates singleton classes as MRB_TT_SCLASS (src/class.c:371), so the check would reject them
type_check_refused.T_FIXNUM: mruby has one integer tag (MRB_TT_INTEGER, include/mruby/value.h:144); CRuby's Fixnum range is not mruby's integer range, and mruby's bignum tag is MRB_TT_BIGINT (value.h:165)
type_check_refused.T_BIGNUM: mruby's bignum tag MRB_TT_BIGINT (include/mruby/value.h:165) is chosen by mruby's integer width, not CRuby's Fixnum/Bignum boundary, so the tags do not select the same values
type_check_refused.T_NIL: nil and false share mruby's tag MRB_TT_FALSE (include/mruby/value.h:245-248; mrb_nil_p tells them apart by value), so a type check cannot tell nil from false
type_check_refused.T_FALSE: mruby's MRB_TT_FALSE (include/mruby/value.h:245-248) also matches nil, which CRuby reports as T_NIL
type_check_refused.T_TRUE: not in the type-check subset of this change (refused as listed); mruby's MRB_TT_TRUE (value.h:251) is true only, so it can be added as its own change
type_check_refused.T_UNDEF: CRuby's Qundef is an internal marker, not a Ruby object type; mruby's MRB_TT_UNDEF is a separate value kind
type_check_refused.T_STRUCT: mruby's MRB_TT_STRUCT (include/mruby/value.h:160) is not documented as the type of Struct instances, so the match is not verified
type_check_refused.T_REGEXP: mruby has no core Regexp type tag (none in include/mruby/value.h:138-167), so there is no fixed tag to compare with
type_check_refused.T_RATIONAL: mruby's MRB_TT_RATIONAL (include/mruby/value.h:164) is a gem type; the match with CRuby's Rational is not verified
type_check_refused.T_COMPLEX: mruby's MRB_TT_COMPLEX (include/mruby/value.h:163) is a gem type; the match with CRuby's Complex is not verified

rb_const_get_at.reason: no exact mruby equivalent: mrb_const_get also searches the superclass chain, rb_const_get_at looks only in the receiver

rb_ensure.reason: no direct mruby equivalent (ensure callback not in the supported subset)

rb_rescue.reason: no direct mruby equivalent (rescue callback not in the supported subset)

rb_rescue2.reason: no direct mruby equivalent (rescue callback not in the supported subset)

rb_gc_register_address.reason: address form (VALUE *): mruby has no address root. mrb_gc_register roots a value, so a later store through the address would not be rooted; the rooting must be designed by hand

rb_gc_register_mark_object.caveat: mrb_gc_register keeps the value in mruby's root table (src/gc.c:564) for the life of the state; CRuby never unregisters it either. Immediate values need no root and are ignored by mrb_gc_register

rb_gc_mark.caveat: valid only inside a data type mark callback (the runtime passes the state); refused elsewhere

rb_gc_mark_movable.reason: no mark callback in mruby: mrb_data_type has only dfree and ivars (include/mruby/data.h), so a mark function would never be called and rb_gc_mark has no place to run (movable marking has no mruby form either)

rb_gc_enable.reason: no mruby enable function: gc.disabled is a VM flag (include/mruby/gc.h), and CRuby's return value (the previous state) would have to be emulated

rb_gc_disable.reason: no mruby disable function: gc.disabled is a VM flag (include/mruby/gc.h), and CRuby's return value (the previous state) would have to be emulated

StringValuePtr.caveat: argument must already be a String: no implicit to_str conversion

StringValueCStr.caveat: argument must already be a String: no to_str conversion and no NUL-byte check

NUM2ULONG.caveat: signed conversion: unsigned range is not checked

rb_str_new_frozen.caveat: returns a copy; the copy is not frozen

rb_thread_call_without_gvl.caveat: modelled on mruby-uv: func runs on the libuv thread pool and the caller runs the loop until it finishes; ubf is ignored (no interrupt)

rb_ext_ractor_safe.reason: ractor declaration; mruby has no ractors, so the declaration has no effect

rb_intern_const.caveat: argument must be a string literal (mrb_intern_lit is a macro over mrb_intern_static); a char pointer does not compile

rb_hash_aset.caveat: mruby returns void; the CRuby return value (the stored value) is not available

rb_ary_push.caveat: mruby returns void; the CRuby return value (the array) is not available

RARRAY_AREF.caveat: CRuby reads the element pointer without a bounds check; mruby returns nil out of range and accepts negative offsets

rb_utf8_str_new.caveat: mruby strings carry no encoding: the bytes are copied unchanged and UTF-8 is not recorded

rb_obj_class.caveat: returns struct RClass *, not mrb_value: wrap with mrb_obj_value() where a VALUE is needed

rb_respond_to.caveat: returns mrb_bool (0 or 1), where CRuby returns int

rb_ivar_set.caveat: mruby returns void; the CRuby return value (the value) is not available

INT2FIX.caveat: no range check: the mruby fixnum range depends on the value boxing

LONG2FIX.caveat: no range check: the mruby fixnum range depends on the value boxing

FIX2INT.caveat: no check that the value is a fixnum; the result is mrb_int, not int

FIX2LONG.caveat: no check that the value is a fixnum; the result is mrb_int

rb_type.caveat: returns enum mrb_vtype: compare only with MRB_TT_* values. nil and false both report MRB_TT_FALSE (mruby/boxing_nan.h), so T_NIL and T_FALSE are not mapped

Qundef.caveat: mrb_value is a struct: test with mrb_undef_p(), not with ==

T_OBJECT.caveat: CRuby T_OBJECT also covers exception objects, which mruby types as MRB_TT_EXCEPTION (src/error.c:42); RB_TYPE_P and Check_Type do not match them, so T_OBJECT is refused in both

T_CLASS.caveat: mruby types singleton classes as MRB_TT_SCLASS (src/class.c:371) and CRuby reports them as T_CLASS, so T_CLASS is refused in both RB_TYPE_P and Check_Type

T_DATA.caveat: CRuby T_DATA also covers TypedData; MRB_TT_CDATA is the nearest mruby C-data type, so check each use

rb_global_variable.reason: address form (VALUE *), as rb_gc_register_address: no mruby equivalent (mrb_gc_register roots a value, not a variable)

rb_str_cat.caveat: the length is not checked for sign: a negative length becomes a large size_t

rb_str_buf_new.caveat: capa is a size hint only: the new string is empty, as in CRuby

rb_utf8_str_new_cstr.caveat: mruby strings carry no encoding: the bytes are copied unchanged and UTF-8 is not recorded

rb_str_freeze.caveat: mrb_obj_freeze freezes any object; CRuby's rb_str_freeze takes a String

rb_str_append.caveat: no encoding compatibility check (mruby has no encodings); CRuby raises Encoding::CompatibilityError for incompatible encodings

RHASH_SIZE.caveat: returns mrb_int (signed), where CRuby returns size_t

NUM2DBL.caveat: needs float support (not MRB_NO_FLOAT); nil and non-numeric values raise TypeError as in CRuby, with mruby's message

rb_num2dbl.caveat: needs float support (not MRB_NO_FLOAT); nil and non-numeric values raise TypeError as in CRuby, with mruby's message

ULONG2NUM.caveat: no range check: an unsigned value above the mrb_int maximum wraps negative

ULL2NUM.caveat: no range check: an unsigned value above the mrb_int maximum wraps negative

NUM2LL.caveat: mrb_int may be narrower than long long: values outside its range are not preserved

rb_id2name.caveat: the pointer is into mruby's symbol table: valid until the state is closed

rb_id2str.caveat: mruby does not promise a frozen result, as CRuby's rb_id2str does

rb_to_id.caveat: accepts only Symbol and String: CRuby also converts other objects with to_str

rb_block_given_p.caveat: returns mrb_bool (0 or 1), where CRuby returns int

rb_const_defined.caveat: a module receiver does not fall back to Object, as in rb_const_get; returns mrb_bool

rb_const_defined_at.caveat: returns mrb_bool, where CRuby returns int

RB_LIKELY.caveat: the branch-prediction hint is dropped; !!(x) has the same 0 or 1 value as the GCC definition of RB_LIKELY

RB_UNLIKELY.caveat: the branch-prediction hint is dropped; !!(x) has the same 0 or 1 value as the GCC definition of RB_UNLIKELY

rb_class2name.caveat: CRuby first skips singleton and include classes (rb_class_real); mrb_class_name does not. An anonymous class gets a new name string, and the pointer into it can dangle after the next GC (a named class keeps its path string alive)

rb_define_alias.caveat: the class is a struct RClass * (as rb_undef_method): a class variable is passed unwrapped, and a VALUE there would not type-check. Names are C strings with the new name first (as in CRuby); the original must exist, as in CRuby (NameError)

rb_undef_method.caveat: the first argument is a struct RClass *, not a VALUE; a class variable there is passed unwrapped (special_arg_positions_class_only)

SYM2ID.caveat: no check that the value is a Symbol; the result is mrb_sym (the mapped type of ID), not an unsigned long

T_FALSE.caveat: mruby's nil also has type MRB_TT_FALSE (mrb_nil_p tells them apart by value), so this matches nil, which CRuby reports as T_NIL; RB_TYPE_P(x, T_FALSE) stays refused for this reason

RUBY_T_FIXNUM.caveat: mruby has no bignum, so MRB_TT_INTEGER matches every Integer, including values CRuby reports as T_BIGNUM; RB_TYPE_P(x, T_FIXNUM) stays refused for this reason

T_FIXNUM.caveat: mruby has no bignum, so MRB_TT_INTEGER matches every Integer, including values CRuby reports as T_BIGNUM; RB_TYPE_P(x, T_FIXNUM) stays refused for this reason

rb_eIndexError.caveat: struct RClass *, as E_ARGUMENT_ERROR: a VALUE use needs mrb_obj_value(); in rb_raise it is the class argument

rb_eRangeError.caveat: struct RClass *, as E_ARGUMENT_ERROR: a VALUE use needs mrb_obj_value(); in rb_raise it is the class argument

rb_warn.caveat: prints on every call; CRuby's rb_warn is silent when $VERBOSE is nil. Output is 'warning: ' and the message on stderr, with no file or line; PRIsVALUE is not supported

rb_sys_fail.caveat: raises SystemCallError (with the errno) only when mruby-errno defines it; otherwise RuntimeError with the message, which mruby does not allow to be NULL

rb_obj_classname.caveat: an anonymous class gets a new name string, and the pointer into it can dangle after the next GC (a named class keeps its path string alive), as for rb_class2name

rb_sym2id.caveat: no check that the value is a Symbol; the result is mrb_sym (the mapped type of ID), not an unsigned long

rb_warning.caveat: prints on every call: CRuby's rb_warning prints only in verbose mode ($VERBOSE true), and rb_warn always prints. Output is 'warning: ' and the message on stderr, with no file or line; PRIsVALUE is not supported

rb_gc_location.caveat: identity: mruby's collector never moves objects (no relocation API in include/ or src/gc.c), so the location is the value itself; the argument stays in parentheses

rb_str_buf_cat.caveat: CRuby's rb_str_buf_cat is an alias of rb_str_cat (ruby/internal/intern/string.h:1680); the length is not checked for sign: a negative length becomes a large size_t

rb_usascii_str_new.caveat: mruby strings carry no encoding: the bytes are copied unchanged and US-ASCII is not recorded

rb_usascii_str_new_cstr.caveat: mruby strings carry no encoding: the bytes are copied unchanged and US-ASCII is not recorded

rb_usascii_str_new2.caveat: CRuby's rb_usascii_str_new2 is an alias of rb_usascii_str_new_cstr (ruby/internal/intern/string.h:1679); mruby strings carry no encoding, so US-ASCII is not recorded

rb_ll2inum.caveat: mrb_int may be narrower than long long: values outside its range are not preserved

NUM2UINT.caveat: signed conversion: the unsigned int range is not checked, and the result is mrb_int, not unsigned int

NUM2SIZET.caveat: signed conversion: the size_t range is not checked, and the result is mrb_int, not size_t

FIX2ULONG.caveat: no check that the value is a fixnum; the result is mrb_int, not unsigned long

OBJ_FREEZE.caveat: CRuby's OBJ_FREEZE (rb_obj_freeze_inline, ruby/internal/fl_type.h:911) returns void; mruby's mrb_obj_freeze returns the object, which a statement use discards

rb_obj_is_kind_of.caveat: returns mrb_bool (0 or 1), where CRuby returns VALUE (Qtrue or Qfalse); the class argument is a struct RClass * (a class variable is passed unwrapped: special_arg_positions_class_only), so a VALUE class does not type-check

rb_obj_id.caveat: returns mrb_int, where CRuby returns an Integer VALUE: wrap with mrb_int_value(mrb, ...) where a VALUE is needed. mruby's id is the object's address (src/etc.c), CRuby's is a sequence number: both are unique among live objects, but the values differ

CLASS_OF.caveat: returns struct RClass *, where CRuby's CLASS_OF returns VALUE: wrap with mrb_obj_value() where a VALUE is needed

rb_class_of.caveat: returns struct RClass *, where CRuby's rb_class_of returns VALUE (ruby/internal/globals.h:174): wrap with mrb_obj_value() where a VALUE is needed

rb_include_module.caveat: both arguments are struct RClass * (class variables are passed unwrapped: special_arg_positions_class_only), so a VALUE class or module does not type-check; cyclic includes raise ArgumentError in both

rb_eFrozenError.caveat: struct RClass *, as E_ARGUMENT_ERROR: a VALUE use needs mrb_obj_value(); in rb_raise it is the class argument

RTYPEDDATA_DATA.caveat: both read the data field of a VALUE and are lvalues. mruby has no typed/untyped split: the object must be an mruby data object (mrb_data_type), and the type is not checked, as in CRuby

RB_INTEGER_TYPE_P.caveat: mruby has no bignum: MRB_TT_INTEGER matches every Integer, including values CRuby reports as a bignum (the same reason RUBY_T_FIXNUM is caveated)

rb_define_private_method.caveat: registers a private method: the same wrapper and argument spec as rb_define_method (mrb_define_private_method has the same shape); the method is callable only without a receiver, as in CRuby

rb_iv_get.caveat: the name must be a string literal: it is interned with mrb_intern_cstr at each call; CRuby checks the name is an ivar name, mruby does not

rb_iv_set.caveat: the name must be a string literal: it is interned with mrb_intern_cstr at each call; CRuby checks the name is an ivar name, mruby does not

rb_protect.caveat: the function is called with the mruby state (mrb_func_t: mrb, then the data), so a callback passed here is threaded with an mrb argument (helper threading); the state argument is int * in CRuby but mrb_bool * in mruby, so a caller variable must be declared mrb_bool; only mruby exceptions are caught, and CRuby errinfo is not set

rb_class_new_instance.caveat: the arguments are reordered: CRuby rb_class_new_instance(argc, argv, klass) is mruby mrb_obj_new(mrb, klass, argc, argv); the class must be a tracked class variable (struct RClass *); both calls run initialize

rb_hash_lookup.caveat: returns nil when the key is missing (mrb_hash_fetch with a nil default), as CRuby does; the hash must be a Hash VALUE

rb_sym2str.caveat: the Symbol VALUE is converted with mrb_symbol; mruby does not promise a frozen result, as CRuby does

rb_cstr_to_inum.caveat: the C string becomes a String (mrb_str_new_cstr) and mrb_str_to_inum parses it; base and badcheck keep their order; the result is an Integer VALUE

rb_gv_get.caveat: the name must be a string literal: it is interned with mrb_intern_cstr at each call; special globals may behave differently in mruby

rb_gv_set.caveat: the name must be a string literal: it is interned with mrb_intern_cstr at each call; special globals may behave differently in mruby

rb_reg_nth_match.caveat: match[nth] on the OnigMatchData of the gem (api_map: onig regexp API), nil for a nil match, as CRuby does; the match is an OnigMatchData, not a MatchData

rb_backref_get.caveat: reads $~, which the onig gem sets when its @set_global_variables flag is on; otherwise it is nil

rb_backref_set.caveat: writes $~ (the onig gem reads it back through its last-match variable); the value is the match, as CRuby stores it

rb_match_busy.reason: a hint that keeps a match object from being reused; mruby has no match cache to keep, so the call has no effect

rb_jump_tag.caveat: re-raises the exception that mrb_protect caught (mrb->exc); CRuby's state argument is not needed, and the state is ignored

RUBY_TYPED_FREE_IMMEDIATELY.caveat: mruby has no typed-data flags: free timing and the write-barrier flag are not represented; 0 keeps the initializer shape

RUBY_TYPED_WB_PROTECTED.caveat: mruby has no typed-data flags: free timing and the write-barrier flag are not represented; 0 keeps the initializer shape

RUBY_TYPED_EMBEDDABLE.caveat: mruby has no typed-data flags: free timing and the write-barrier flag are not represented; 0 keeps the initializer shape

rb_data_typed_object_wrap.caveat: wraps the C pointer in a data object of the given mrb_data_type; the class must be a tracked class variable (struct RClass *)

TypedData_Wrap_Struct.caveat: CRuby TypedData_Wrap_Struct(klass, type, sval) reordered to mrb_data_object_alloc(mrb, klass, sval, type)

TypedData_Make_Struct.caveat: allocates a zeroed struct with mrb_calloc (freed by the type dfree), as CRuby does; the struct pointer is assigned to the last argument

TypedData_Get_Struct.caveat: reads the data pointer with mrb_data_get_ptr, which raises TypeError on a mismatched type, as CRuby does

rb_hash_foreach.caveat: the callback gets (mrb, key, value, void *): its third VALUE parameter is the pointer it is given; a callback result of 0 continues and non-zero breaks (ST_CONTINUE and ST_STOP); ST_DELETE is refused because mruby would break the loop on it

ST_CONTINUE.caveat: mrb_hash_foreach continues while the callback returns 0

ST_STOP.caveat: mrb_hash_foreach breaks on any non-zero result, so ST_STOP (1) stops the loop as in CRuby

RBIMPL_ATTR_NORETURN.reason: a no-return attribute: a hint for the compiler that mruby does not need; the declaration has the same meaning without it
